title: AI-assisted analysis reveals retrospective seismicity before the Dingri earthquake
summary: A PhaseNet-assisted workflow combined phase detection, polarisation analysis and template matching on records from one permanent station to reconstruct seismicity in the two years before the 2025 Mw 7.1 Dingri earthquake. The authors report increased event rate and clustering beginning about 45 days before the mainshock. This retrospective pattern is interpreted as compatible with late-stage nucleation; the study does not establish a prospective earthquake forecast.
ai_technology: PhaseNet deep neural-network seismic phase picker combined with polarisation analysis and template matching
organization: Istituto Nazionale di Oceanografia e di Geofisica Sperimentale (OGS)

evidence.tested: PhaseNet-assisted phase detection, polarisation analysis and template matching reconstructed 289 template events and 1,138 augmented events at one station before the 2025 Dingri earthquake. The authors report increased event rate and clustering beginning about 45 days before the mainshock.
evidence.unknown: This is a retrospective analysis from one station. The authors describe a pattern compatible with late-stage nucleation; it does not establish a prospective forecast or earthquake prediction.
evidence.ai_role: PhaseNet, a deep neural-network phase picker, supported detection and event-catalogue construction; the resulting catalogue enabled retrospective identification of the pre-mainshock activity increase.

source_review.scope: Primary Scientific Reports indexed article, including abstract, Methods, Results, article dates and author-affiliation block.
